---
title: "Reshaping Iris Measurements with pivot_longer()"
author: "Ummay Rukiya"
format: html
---

## Why reshape the data?

I wanted to find the average length and width of the sepals and petals for each iris species. In the built-in `iris` dataset, each flower has its own row, but the four measurements are in four separate columns. That layout works well if I want to look at one flower at a time. To summarize the measurements with the same code, I used `pivot_longer()` to turn those four columns into rows.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

iris_wide <- iris |>
  mutate(flower_id = row_number(), .before = 1)

head(iris_wide, 3)
```

I added a flower ID before reshaping so I can still tell which measurements came from the same flower.

## Turn measurement columns into rows

```{r}
iris_long <- iris_wide |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, Petal.Length, Petal.Width),
    names_to = c("part", "dimension"),
    names_sep = "[.]",
    values_to = "measurement_cm"
  )

head(iris_long, 8)
```

The `cols` argument tells R which columns to reshape. With `names_to` and `names_sep`, I split each old column name at the period. For example, `Sepal.Length` becomes `Sepal` in the `part` column and `Length` in the `dimension` column. The actual value goes into `measurement_cm`, while the flower ID and species stay with each measurement.

```{r}
c(wide_rows = nrow(iris_wide), long_rows = nrow(iris_long))
```

The number of rows goes from 150 to 600 because each flower now has four rows, one for each measurement. They still represent the same 150 flowers.

## Summarize the measurements

```{r}
iris_summary <- iris_long |>
  group_by(Species, part, dimension) |>
  summarize(
    flowers = n_distinct(flower_id),
    average_cm = round(mean(measurement_cm), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(iris_summary, n = 12)
```

I grouped by species, flower part, and dimension so I could compare lengths and widths separately. For example, the average petal length is about 1.46 cm for setosa and 5.55 cm for virginica in this dataset. What I found useful about the long format is that I could calculate all 12 averages with one summary.
